guide.headline: Sayin and Smith shredded Iowa through the air
guide.hook: Ohio State's top-tier quarterback and the nation's most explosive young receiver turned Iowa's banged-up pass defense into a track meet.

items.title: Sayin picks apart the deep shell
items.what: Julian Sayin finished 20 of 27 for 324 yards and three touchdowns, building on a season line of 1206 yards, 10 touchdowns, and just 1 interception at 10.5 yards an attempt. Ohio State ranks top 2 percent of FBS quarterbacks in that profile, and against Iowa he looked every bit of it, throwing with rhythm and getting the ball outside the numbers in stride.
items.when: Watch every first-down dropback in the first half.

items.title: Smith wins over the top again
items.what: Jeremiah Smith caught 11 passes for 206 yards and two touchdowns in this game, pushing his season totals to 33 catches, 617 yards, and 7 touchdowns at 18.7 yards a reception, top 1 percent of FBS receivers. Ohio State came in ranked No. 61 of 138 in pass explosiveness while Iowa ranked No. 122 of 138 at stopping it, a 44 percentile point gap, and Smith is exactly how that gap gets exploited.
items.when: Watch the first deep shot of the game and whether Iowa rolls a safety over after it.

items.title: Third-and-long was no problem
items.what: Ohio State throws on 85 percent of third-and-long situations, 17 of 20 snaps, and converts 45 percent of the time, No. 6 of 133 nationally. Iowa had been solid there, allowing just a 19 percent conversion rate, No. 39 of 136, but Sayin's efficiency and Smith's catch radius made those down-and-distance numbers look irrelevant on replay.
items.when: Watch any third-and-7-or-more snap in the second and third quarters.

guide.cardLine: Julian Sayin threw for 324 yards and three scores while Jeremiah Smith went for 206 yards and two touchdowns against Iowa's exposed secondary.
